cards.text: This psalm is from Asaph, a Levite musician who led worship in David's day (1 Chronicles 16:4-5). It's written for the choirmaster. Asaph opens with a call to God's people, and friend, it is NOT a quiet one.

cards.question: Asaph opens by calling God's people to sing for joy to God.

cards.text: And he wants the WHOLE band: a song, the tambourine, the harp and the lyre. I sing to my ovens every morning, and not ONE of them has ever asked for an encore.

cards.question: Next Asaph calls for the ram's horn, and he ties it to the calendar. When should it sound?

answers.text: At the New Moon and the full moon
On the first day of the harvest

cards.question: Asaph gives a reason for all this noise on the feast day. What is it?

answers.text: God made it a statute for Israel

cards.text: Asaph says God set it up as a testimony for Joseph. So this isn't just a party, friend, it's a party with a MEMORY, and that memory goes back to a land Israel knew all too well.

cards.question: This testimony for Joseph goes back to the land of ___.

cards.text: Back over the land of Egypt, the psalm says, "I heard an unfamiliar language" there. Then the words switch, and now it's God talking, and He's looking back at His people carrying heavy loads.

cards.question: God remembers the burden on His people's shoulder. What does He say He did about it?

cards.text: You know the one-trip-from-the-car move, every bag on both arms, fingers turning PURPLE? Now picture all of it lifted off, because God says their hands were freed from the basket.
And God keeps remembering. His people called out to Him in distress, and you know that voice, friend. It's the one I use when the timer's going off and my mustache can't find the oven mitt.

cards.question: When His people called out in distress, God says He ___ them.
God says He answered His people from a cloud of thunder.

cards.text: Then God names a place: the waters of Meribah, where the people once quarreled over water (Exodus 17:1-7). I once watched the dead batteries I shared a drawer with argue for a WEEK over who had the most charge left, so I get it.

cards.question: What does God say happened at the waters of Meribah?

cards.text: After a Selah, God opens with "Hear, O My people, and I will warn you" and friend, when ANYBODY opens like that, you put the phone DOWN.

cards.question: God says He wishes His people would listen to Him.
God warns Israel about one thing that must never be among them. What is it?

cards.text: Then God reminds them who's talking: the LORD their God, who brought them up out of Egypt. And He says, "Open wide your mouth, and I will fill it."

cards.question: When God tells Israel to open wide their mouth so He can fill it, what is He offering?

answers.text: To give them what they need
To teach them a new song

cards.question: After an offer like that, God says His people listened and obeyed Him.
Israel won't listen to God. So what does God do?

answers.text: Gives them up to their stubborn hearts

cards.text: Oof, that one stings. But God isn't done, and here comes that wish again: if only His people would listen, if Israel would follow His ways.

cards.question: If Israel would follow His ways, God says He'd soon turn His hand against their ___.

cards.text: Then God turns to those who hate the LORD. And what He says about how they'd act sent both of my bushy eyebrows straight UP.

cards.question: God says those who hate the LORD would truly obey Him.

cards.text: Those who hate the LORD would only feign obedience, like the coworker who looks SO busy the second the boss walks by. And God says their doom would last forever.
How does God close out this psalm, friend? Not with enemies but with feeding His people, and you KNOW that's my favorite part.

cards.question: If only His people would listen, what does God say He would feed them?

cards.text: And with honey from the rock, God says He would satisfy them. Honey from a ROCK, friend, and I've stared at plenty of rocks without a single one ever handing me a thing.

findings.problem: Joseph is named for the first time without any simple identification of who he is.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The first-person quotation is introduced only with "the psalm says," so the card never identifies who the speaker of "I heard an unfamiliar language" is before quoting it.

rule.text: When he quotes someone speaking as "I," he says who it is first.

findings.problem: This non-opening story card has three sentences: "And God keeps remembering," the sentence about the people calling out, and the oven-mitt sentence.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: "After an offer like that" points back to the preceding cards without saying what the offer was, so the question does not supply its own context.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: Neither card 8 nor any earlier card introduces enemies or a promise of victory. The baker therefore cannot reason out "foes"; the blank simply asks for wording from verse 14 that has not yet been shown.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The setup says only that God would feed His people, with nothing that distinguishes the finest wheat from manna or quail. This is another unseen-detail guess in a stop that already uses several discovery picks, rather than a choice the baker can reason through.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer. A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.
